source.title: Tracker
source.description: Where the tickets are read from and created. The code is always on GitHub.

repo.title: Repository
repo.description: The GitHub repository the release changes, owner/name

base_branch.title: Base branch
base_branch.description: The branch the plan reads and every pull request targets (for example dev)

ticket.title: Ticket
ticket.description: An existing GitHub issue to plan, such as acme/payments#42. Leave empty to describe a goal instead.

goal.title: Goal
goal.description: What the release should achieve, in your words. Added to the ticket when both are given.

def.description: Read the ticket from GitHub, or plan from the goal alone.
Read the GitHub issue and its first comments.
No ticket to read - the goal is the request. Marks that branch for the join below.
The ticket as one plain ticket (key, title, description).
The request as one brief - the ticket, then any direction typed as the goal.
Read the repository and prepare the conversation before planning - the questions only a person can answer and two or three approaches with one recommended (brainstorm-requirements skill).

A person answers the questions and picks an approach before the release is planned; rejecting stops the run with nothing planned. Answer in mission control, with azhi approve, or from the Slack approval message.

message.cel: 'Before the release is planned: ' + nodes.brainstorm.output.summary + ' Answer the ' + string(size(nodes.brainstorm.output.questions)) + ' question(s) and choose an approach, or reject to stop.'

approach.title: Approach
approach.description: The name of the approach to plan, as listed (or your own direction in a few words).

answers.title: Answers
answers.description: One answer per question, in order. Leave a question's answer empty to take its recommendation. They are treated as decisions by the planner.

def.description: Read the repository and write the release plan - problem, scope, invariants, user journeys and up to three epics (release-prd skill).
The release plan as Markdown, for the approver.
A person approves the release plan before any ticket is created, and may leave epics out. Answer in mission control, with azhi approve, or from the Slack approval message.

message.cel: 'Approve the release plan "' + nodes.plan_release.output.title + '" and split its ' + string(size(nodes.plan_release.output.epics)) + ' epic(s) into tickets? Name the epics to leave out, if any.'

drop.title: Epics to leave out
drop.description: Epic numbers from the plan, for example 2,3. Leave empty to split them all.

def.description: The text of each epic the splitter receives, with the release context in front (epics the approver left out are removed).
Is there an epic to split? A plan whose epics were all left out ends here, with nothing to deliver.
Run the published issue-splitter on this round's epic. It waits for a person at its own approval, so it may take days.
The Stories this round's splitter created, or that it failed. Reads the child's output as data and fails closed.

Split each epic with the published issue-splitter (analysis, its own approval, then the Stories), one after the other.

reasons.stop: An epic could not be split

def.description: The Stories in delivery order - epics in plan order, then each epic's Stories as the splitter created them - or why there is nothing to deliver.
Deliver only when every epic was split and there is at least one Story. Otherwise the run goes to the summary.

A person confirms what will be delivered before the first Story starts; rejecting it stops the run with nothing delivered. Answer in mission control, with azhi approve, or from the Slack approval message.

message.cel: 'Deliver ' + string(nodes.order.output.count) + ' Story(ies) from ' + inputs.repo + ' into ' + inputs.base_branch + '? Each becomes a branch stacked on the one before and a pull request into ' + inputs.base_branch + '. Choose the mode: supervised (a person approves the specs of each Story and signs each one off) or auto (the recommendations of the agents are taken where the rules say it is safe, every such decision is posted to Slack, and anything doubtful still asks). Leaving it empty is supervised. Reject to stop with nothing delivered.'

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: supervised: a person approves every Story's specs and signs every Story off. auto: no person is asked at those two points when the rules say it is safe (reviewers approved, tests passed, nothing critical), the agents' recommendations are taken for open questions, and each decision is posted to Slack; anything doubtful still asks. The plan and the tickets were already approved by a person.
